name: HongShan
tagline: China's most systematic AI backer — from foundation models to robot hands and brain-computer interfaces
summary: HongShan is the China business formerly known as Sequoia Capital China, led by Neil Shen. Sequoia announced a three-way split of its global partnership in June 2023 and completed it in March 2024, since when HongShan has been a legally and financially separate partnership from Sequoia Capital in the US and Peak XV Partners in India and Southeast Asia — the portfolio below is HongShan's alone. Its AI programme spans every Chinese frontier model lab, the full embodied-intelligence stack from brains to hands to feet, autonomous driving and vision AI, and a brain-computer interface portfolio it began assembling in 2020.

facts.label: Leadership
facts.value: Neil Shen — founding and managing partner

thesis.heading: Every Chinese frontier lab, concentrated in MiniMax
thesis.body: HongShan holds positions in Moonshot AI, MiniMax, Zhipu AI, Light Years Beyond and StepFun — effectively the full field of Chinese foundation-model contenders. Its heaviest single bet is MiniMax, where it led a US$50M A+ round and kept adding, ending pre-IPO as the third largest financial shareholder at 3.81%.

thesis.heading: Back early, then add on proof
thesis.body: The firm's seed vehicle entered Unitree Robotics at Pre-A in December 2019 with RMB 15M at a RMB 150M post-money valuation, then followed nearly every round to a 7.11% stake worth over RMB 2.5B on paper — the seed fund's first investment and the template for how HongShan compounds early conviction.

thesis.heading: Embodied intelligence as a jigsaw
thesis.body: Rather than picking one robot winner, HongShan funded each layer of the stack: the brain (AgiBot), perception (Mech-Mind), hands (LinkerBot), feet (Lingzu Tech), force-controlled arms (Agile Robots), warehouse and consumer robots (Hai Robotics, Narwal, AgileX) and rehabilitation robotics (Fourier).

thesis.heading: Brain-computer interfaces, five years early
thesis.body: From 2020 the firm systematically backed Neuracle, NeuroXess, Zhiran Medical and SceneRay, entering a category most institutional investors only discovered around 2025 and holding it with unusually long patience.
